statement: The permutation and orientation conventions. Let $X_g$ be a closed connected orientable topological surface and $S_n\subset X_g$ a specified $n$-element set. Give its homeomorphism group the compact-open topology on a homeomorphism and its inverse, and put $U_{g,n}=X_g\setminus S_n$. Then \[ 1\longrightarrow A^!_{g,n}\longrightarrow A_{g,n} \longrightarrow\mathfrak S_n\longrightarrow1, \qquad 1\longrightarrow\pi_0(A^!_{g,n})\longrightarrow M^{\pm}_{g,n} \longrightarrow\mathfrak S_n\longrightarrow1. \] The orientation character $\epsilon:M^{\pm}_{g,n}\to\{\pm1\}$ is surjective and its kernel is $M^+_{g,n}$. The intersection of the permutation and orientation kernels is $P_{g,n}$. In particular the manuscript's unadorned group is neither pure nor orientation-preserving by definition. ; the positive superscript is specified in \S19, folio 113, scan 226.

statement: Surface groups with peripheral structure. Choose an orientation, a base point $b\in U_{g,n}$, and paths to small positively oriented puncture circles. Then \[ \Pi_{g,n}=\left\langle a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_g,b_g,c_1,\ldots,c_n\ \middle|\ \prod_{i=1}^g[a_i,b_i]\prod_{j=1}^nc_j=1\right\rangle. \] For $n>0$ this is free of rank $2g+n-1$. For hyperbolic type it is centre-free and residually finite. Its peripheral datum consists of the conjugacy classes of the cyclic subgroups $\langle c_j\rangle$, with the coherent orientation datum; for $n=0$ we retain the orientation line in $H_2(\Pi_{g,0},\mathbb Z)$. The Dehn--Nielsen--Baer identification is \[ M^{\pm}_{g,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(\Pi_{g,n}). \] The target preserves the peripheral classes as a set; restricting to fixed classes and multiplier $+1$ gives $P_{g,n}$. ; see \citet[Theorems 8.1 and 8.8]{AF_FarbMargalit2012}.

statement: Filling one point and the precise Birman group. For a hyperbolic target $U_{g,n}$ and one extra point $b$, let $M^{\pm}_{g,n+1,*}$ be the subgroup fixing that extra point, while allowing the old punctures to be permuted. There are exact sequences of discrete groups \[ 1\longrightarrow\Pi_{g,n}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{push}} M^{\pm}_{g,n+1,*}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{forget}}M^{\pm}_{g,n}\longrightarrow1, \qquad 1\longrightarrow\Pi_{g,n}\longrightarrow P_{g,n+1}\longrightarrow P_{g,n}\longrightarrow1. \] There is no forgetting homomorphism on the full group that permits the extra point itself to be permuted. On fundamental groups the inclusion of opens instead gives the surjection $\Pi_{g,n+1}\to\Pi_{g,n}$ killing the normal closure of the last peripheral loop. These are different maps between different groups. ; \citet[Theorem 4.6]{AF_FarbMargalit2012}.

statement: A covering gives a correspondence with specified lifts. Let $p:U'\to U$ be a connected finite unramified covering of orientable finite-type surfaces, with $U$ hyperbolic. A choice of points above $b$ identifies $\pi_1(U')$ with a finite-index subgroup $H<\Pi=\pi_1(U)$. Put $L_H=\Stab_{M^{\pm}(U)}([H])$, where $[H]$ denotes conjugacy in $\Pi$. The group of isotopy classes of pairs of commuting lifts $(f',f)$ fits into \[ 1\longrightarrow N_\Pi(H)/H\longrightarrow\mathrm{Lift}(p) \longrightarrow L_H\longrightarrow1, \qquad \mathrm{Lift}(p)\longrightarrow M^{\pm}(U'). \] Thus the general covering operation in the tower is a correspondence, not a canonical homomorphism from all of $M^{\pm}(U)$ to $M^{\pm}(U')$. It preserves the sign of orientation and the induced peripheral subgroups. The degree $d=[\Pi:H]$ satisfies $2g'-2+n'=d(2g-2+n)$.

statement: The modular object retains isotropy. For a stable labelled type, the analytic moduli stack is $[\mathcal T_{g,n}/P_{g,n}]$, with $\mathcal T_{g,n}$ contractible; the unordered stack is $[\mathcal T_{g,n}/M^+_{g,n}]$. Consequently its geometric \emph{stack} fundamental group is respectively $\widehat P_{g,n}$ or $\widehat{M^+_{g,n}}$. The manuscript's $M_{g,n}$ in (19)--(25), scans 326--329, corresponds to the unordered version: (20) explicitly has $\widehat{\mathcal T}^+_{g,n}$, not $\widehat{\mathcal T}^{!+}_{g,n}$. In particular $\mathscr M_{0,3}=\Spec\mathbb Q$ but $\mathscr M_{0,[3]}\simeq B\mathfrak S_3$.

statement: Arithmetic fundamental-group and universal-monodromy sequences. Fix $\overline{\mathbb Q}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$ and compatible geometric base points on the unordered moduli stack and its universal punctured curve $\mathscr U$. For hyperbolic type, \[ 1\longrightarrow\widehat{M^+_{g,n}}\longrightarrow A^{\mathrm{arith}}_{g,n}:=\pi_1^{\et}(\mathscr M_{g,[n]}) \longrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow1, \] \[ 1\longrightarrow\pi_{g,n}\longrightarrow\pi_1^{\et}(\mathscr U) \longrightarrow A^{\mathrm{arith}}_{g,n}\longrightarrow1. \] Conjugation on the normal geometric fibre defines a commutative diagram to \[ 1\longrightarrow\pi_{g,n}\longrightarrow \Aut_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi_{g,n})\longrightarrow O_{g,n}\longrightarrow1. \] The last sequence uses $Z(\pi_{g,n})=1$. The induced map $\rho_{g,n}:A^{\mathrm{arith}}_{g,n}\to O_{g,n}$ is genuine after these choices; its change under base-point transport is conjugation in $O_{g,n}$. Its geometric restriction need not be identified with an injection before the congruence problem is settled.

statement: A completion is not its image. The discrete action induces a continuous surjection \[ \widehat{M^+_{g,n}}\twoheadrightarrow \Sigma_{g,n}:=\overline{\rho_{g,n}(M^+_{g,n})}\subset O_{g,n}. \] The kernel is the congruence kernel. The double hat in the manuscript denotes the ambient automorphism group $O_{g,n}$, not the profinite completion of $\widehat{M^+_{g,n}}$. In all formulae for stabilizers or normalizers inside $O_{g,n}$, it is the image $\Sigma$ that can be used without the congruence hypothesis.

statement: The quotient sets behind the terminology. Let $\pi$ be a profinite group with the loop structure of $\widehat\Pi_{g,n}$. Write $I(\pi)=\Isom_{\mathrm{lac}}(\widehat\Pi_{g,n},\pi)$ and $I^{\mathrm{out}}(\pi)=I(\pi)/\Inn(\pi)$. Actual discretifications are the images of $\Pi_{g,n}$ under elements of $I(\pi)$, with their transported loop structures. Their based parameter set is \[ \mathrm{Discr}(\pi)=I(\pi)/\Aut_{\mathrm{lac}}(\Pi_{g,n}). \] After taking inner-conjugacy classes, the denominator is $M^{\pm}_{g,n}$. Pre-discretifications replace this discrete denominator by its closure. If $\Sigma^{\pm}=\overline{M^{\pm}_{g,n}}\subset O_{g,n}$, the outer quotient sets are \[ \mathrm{Pre}(\pi)=I^{\mathrm{out}}(\pi)/\Sigma^{\pm}, \qquad \mathrm{Pre}^{+}(\pi)=I^{\mathrm{out}}(\pi)/\Sigma. \] The maps from discretifications to pre-discretifications are quotient maps, not identifications of dense subgroups. Oriented pre-discretifications map two-to-one to unoriented ones for hyperbolic type. ; \S29, folios 188--189, scans 371--374.

statement: Two different groups called $N$, and two different conjectures. For a chosen geometric subgroup $\Sigma\subset O$, define \[ N^{\mathrm{norm}}=N_O(\Sigma),\qquad \mathfrak G^{\mathrm{norm}}=N^{\mathrm{norm}}/\Sigma. \] These are the \S26 definitions. In \S29 the manuscript defines instead \[ N^{\mathrm{arith}}=\rho(A^{\mathrm{arith}}),\qquad \mathfrak G^{\mathrm{arith}}=N^{\mathrm{arith}}/\Sigma. \] There is an inclusion $N^{\mathrm{arith}}\subseteq N^{\mathrm{norm}}$, and a canonical continuous surjection $G_{\mathbb Q}\twoheadrightarrow\mathfrak G^{\mathrm{arith}}$ once the algebraic closure and the arithmetic marking have been fixed. The statement that this surjection is injective does not assert that $N^{\mathrm{arith}}=N^{\mathrm{norm}}$.

statement: The non-hyperbolic types do not satisfy the hyperbolic assertions. The following table refers to punctures, not boundary circles fixed pointwise: \begin{center}\small \begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}\toprule Type & $\Pi$ & $M^+$ & $P$\\\midrule $(0,0)$ & $1$ & $1$ & $1$\\ $(0,1)$ & $1$ & $1$ & $1$\\ $(0,2)$ & $\mathbb Z$ & $\mathbb Z/2$ & $1$\\ $(0,3)$ & $F_2$ & $\mathfrak S_3$ & $1$\\ $(1,0)$ & $\mathbb Z^2$ & $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ & $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$\\ $(1,1)$ & $F_2$ & $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ & $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$\\\bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{center} The extended groups are obtained by including degree $-1$ maps; for $(0,2)$ the result is $(\mathbb Z/2)^2$, and for both torus types it is $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Z)$. The surface group $F_2$ in the last line has peripheral element $[a,b]^{-1}$; the $F_2$ in type $(0,3)$ has three peripheral classes. They are not the same group with loops. Forgetting the marked point on a torus gives an isomorphism of mapping class groups, not a Birman sequence with an injected $\mathbb Z^2$ kernel. ; \S21, folios 129--131, scans 257--261.

statement: Fields, real structures, and characteristics are part of the data. The complex Teichm\"uller tower in this paper consists of orientable surfaces. A non-orientable surface is not the underlying surface of a smooth complex algebraic curve. For a real curve the relevant structure is an extension by $G_{\mathbb R}\simeq\mathbb Z/2$, together with its outer involution on the geometric group; it is not obtained by replacing the curve with the topological quotient by complex conjugation. All arithmetic comparison statements here are in characteristic zero. At primes $2$ and $3$, prime-to-characteristic or tame specialization cannot silently replace the full profinite group, and stack isotropy of orders $2$ and $3$ must be retained.

statement: The three lift extensions and the mixed fundamental group. Assume hyperbolic type and choose the additional base point $b$. Write $A=A^+_{g,n}$, $A_0$ for its identity component, $M=\pi_0A$, and $M_*=\pi_0(A^+_{g,n+1,*})$. The topological pullback \[ \widetilde A=A\times_M M_* \] has the three exact sequences \[ \begin{split} 1&\longrightarrow\Pi_{g,n}\longrightarrow\widetilde A \longrightarrow A\longrightarrow1,\\ 1&\longrightarrow A_0\longrightarrow\widetilde A \longrightarrow M_*\longrightarrow1,\\ 1&\longrightarrow A_0\times\Pi_{g,n}\longrightarrow\widetilde A \longrightarrow M\longrightarrow1. \end{split} \tag{A.1} \] The first extension splits canonically over the subgroup $A_*$ fixing $b$, by lifting maps to fix a chosen point of the universal cover. If $E=EA$ is a universal principal $A$-space (for example the Milnor construction), the associated bundle $\mathcal X=(E\times U_{g,n})/A_0$ has base $E/A_0$ contractible up to homotopy and fibre $U_{g,n}$. Its residual $M$-action has mixed fundamental group \[ \pi_1(\mathcal X\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}M)\simeq M_*, \qquad 1\to\pi_1(U_{g,n})\to M_*\to M\to1. \tag{A.2} \] Here the double slash is the homotopy quotient. These identifications use compatible base points; changing them gives inner conjugation. The same pullback construction applies to the extended groups. , especially (74)--(75), scans 252--254.

statement: The input category, with its variance. Let $n\geq3$, $G_n=P_{0,n}$, and let $\mathcal C_n$ be the set of isotopy classes of essential multicurves on the labelled punctured sphere, including the empty multicurve. For $\sigma\in\mathcal C_n$ put $\Delta_\sigma=\langle t_c:c\in\sigma\rangle\simeq\mathbb Z^{|\sigma|}$. The exit category is \[ \operatorname{Ob}C_n=\mathcal C_n,\qquad \Hom_{C_n}(\sigma,\tau)= \{g\in G_n:g\sigma\supseteq\tau\}/\Delta_\sigma, \qquad [h]\circ[g]=[hg]. \tag{F.1} \] Its nerve is the exit-path $\infty$-category of the boundary-stratified $\overline{\mathscr M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C)$. Put $T_n=C_n^{\op}$. Thus arrows in $C_n$ smooth nodes, arrows in $T_n$ degenerate, and constructible coefficients are covariant functors on $C_n$, or presheaves on $T_n$. This is \citet[Construction 3.18, Proposition 3.23, Corollary 6.6, and Theorem 6.7]{AF_Jansen2023}, with the pure labelled genus-zero convention of A.

statement: A strict, universal finite-category completion. For a category $C$ with a finite specified object set, a finite congruence $R$ is an equivalence relation of finite index on each $\Hom_C(x,y)$ that respects identities and composition. Let $C/R$ retain the same objects and the quotient Hom-sets. The poset of these congruences, ordered by refinement, is cofiltered, and \[ C^{\mathrm{fin}}=(C/R)_R\in\operatorname{Pro}(\mathrm{FinCat}), \qquad C/R'\longrightarrow C/R\quad(R'\subseteq R) \tag{F.2} \] is our strict profinite completion. Every transition functor is the identity on objects and surjective on each Hom-set. Its materialization $|C^{\mathrm{fin}}|=\varprojlim_R C/R$ is a category object in profinite sets with a finite discrete object set. Continuous functors from it to a finite category are precisely the functors represented by the pro-object. Continuous natural isomorphisms are retained, and can be computed at this level. In particular their automorphism groups agree.

statement: Finite representations, split representations, and all continuous representations. For (F.2), finite-valued continuous functors satisfy \[ \Fun_{\cts}(|C^{\mathrm{fin}}|,\mathrm{FinSet}) \simeq\varinjlim_R\Fun(C/R,\mathrm{FinSet}). \tag{F.3} \] For arbitrary sets, the analogous colimit denotes representations that factor through \emph{one} finite stage. It need not contain every continuous representation. For a profinite group $H$, all discrete continuous $H$-sets form the filtered-colimit completion of the finite continuous $H$-sets. They are not the actions of the abstract group with its topology forgotten.

statement: The profinite curve complex and multitwist stabilizers. For genus zero and every $n\geq3$, let $\widehat G_n$ be the full profinite completion. It equals the procongruence completion. The profinite curve complex is defined by embedding an unoriented simple curve in the space of conjugacy classes $\{\gamma,\gamma^{-1}\}$ in $\widehat\Pi_{0,n}$, taking the closure of simple curves, and then taking the closure of the discrete $r$-multicurves in its finite-subset space, for each $r$. Include the empty simplex. It is also the inverse limit of the finite orbit complexes over congruence levels. For a discrete multicurve $\sigma$, its profinite stabilizer is $\overline{H_\sigma}$, where $H_\sigma=\Stab_{G_n}(\sigma)$, and \[ 1\longrightarrow\overline\Delta_\sigma\simeq\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{|\sigma|} \longrightarrow\overline H_\sigma \longrightarrow\prod_v\widehat P_{0,\operatorname{val}(v)}\longrightarrow1. \tag{F.4} \] Furthermore $N_{\widehat G_n}(\overline\Delta_\sigma)=\overline H_\sigma$. The sources are \citet[Definitions 3.3--3.4, Theorems 3.5--3.6, Theorem 4.2, and Corollary 4.3]{Boggi2020BC}, with the genus-zero congruence theorem. The trivial empty-multicurve case is interpreted separately.

statement: Finite quotient categories and the transporter completion agree. For representatives $\sigma_s$ of the stable labelled trees put $A_{st}=\{g\in G_n:g\sigma_s\supseteq\sigma_t\}$. For each finite-index normal subgroup $V\lhd G_n$ let $p_V:G_n\to G_n/V$, and define a finite category $C_{n,V}$ by \[ \operatorname{Ob}C_{n,V}=\{s\},\qquad \Hom_{C_{n,V}}(s,t)=p_V(A_{st})/p_V(\Delta_{\sigma_s}), \quad[h][g]=[hg]. \tag{F.5} \] If $V'\subseteq V$, its transition functor is induced by $G_n/V'\to G_n/V$. These quotient categories are cofinal among all finite congruence quotients of $C_n^0$. Thus \[ \widehat C_n:=\varprojlim_V C_{n,V},\qquad \Hom_{\widehat C_n}(s,t)=\overline{A_{st}}/\overline\Delta_{\sigma_s} \tag{F.6} \] materializes the strict pro-object of F.2. In the full profinite multicurve model this is the candidate transporter formula from the prompt: \[ \Hom(\sigma,\tau)= \{g\in\widehat G_n:g\sigma\supseteq\tau\}/\overline\Delta_\sigma. \] It is a category in profinite sets, and the discrete comparison is faithful for every $n\geq3$.

statement: Forgetting, clutching, and relabelling survive completion. Every specified forgetful functor $Q:C_{n+1}\to C_n$, and every clutching functor, extends to the strict pro-completions by its universal property. On the transporter model, forgetting is induced by the completed pure Birman homomorphism $\widehat\phi:\widehat G_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow\widehat G_n$ and the continuous map on profinite multicurves. In degeneration variance it is $\widehat Q^{\op}:\widehat T_{n+1}\to\widehat T_n$. Relabelling remains a pseudo-action with its specified natural isomorphisms; choosing a skeleton does not manufacture a splitting of a mapping class permutation extension.

statement: Stratified Riemann existence supplies the geometric comparison. Let $X_n=\overline{\mathscr M}_{0,n}$ over $\mathbb Q$, stratified by its stable labelled trees. Fix $\overline{\mathbb Q}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$. The finite boundary-constructible \etale sheaves on $X_{n,\overline{\mathbb Q}}$, with their stalk functors at one chosen geometric point of each stratum, are equivalent to \[ \Fun_{\cts}(\widehat C_n,\mathrm{FinSet}), \tag{F.7} \] with their evaluation functors. The finite-category exodromy object reconstructed from these data is therefore equivalent to the strict completion in F.7. At the full stratified $\infty$-categorical level, the precise theorem is \[ \operatorname{Gal}(X_{n,\mathbb C}/P_n) \simeq\operatorname{Exit}^{P_n}(X_n(\mathbb C))^{\wedge}_{\pi}, \tag{F.8} \] where the right-hand completion is in profinite stratified spaces. Here $P_n$ denotes the finite poset of strata, not the mapping class group $P_{g,n}$. This is \citet[Proposition 12.6.4 and Corollaries 12.6.6--12.6.7]{AF_BGH2020}. We take its finite-category, finite-set exodromy part in (F.7); we do not replace its full $\infty$-categorical completion by a limit of ordinary categories without a further comparison.

statement: Continuous outer Galois action on the completed category. Galois descent defines a coherent continuous action \[ BG_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\widehat C_n) \] in the $2$-category of profinite categories and continuous equivalences. On equivalence classes it gives a homomorphism $G_{\mathbb Q}\to\pi_0\operatorname{Aut}(\widehat C_n)$. It is compatible with forgetting, clutching, and relabelling, and with the opposite category $\widehat T_n$. On a local normal-crossings inertia group at a rational boundary point it acts, modulo simultaneous geometric conjugation, by \[ t_e\longmapsto t_e^{\chi(\sigma)} \quad\text{for every node }e. \tag{F.9} \] For $n\geq4$ the outer action on $\widehat C_n$ is faithful.

statement: The failure of smoothness persists profinitely. For forgetting the fifth marking at the stratum $q_{12,34}$, the continuous lifting groupoid in the STRATA smoothness test is equivalent to $B\widehat{\mathbb Z}$. Its stabilizer is \[ \ker(\widehat\phi)\cap\overline\Delta_q =\{(a,-a):a\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}\} =\overline{\langle t_1t_2^{-1}\rangle}. \tag{F.10} \] Thus the forgetful functor fails the analogous homotopy-smoothness test with continuous finite derived coefficients. Galois preserves this procyclic stabilizer and acts on it by the cyclotomic character, up to simultaneous conjugation.

statement: Restriction to the open stratum detects every categorical automorphism. Let $n\geq4$. A continuous autoequivalence of $\widehat C_n$ fixing the labelled stratum types is determined up to natural isomorphism by its outer action on $\widehat G_n=\Aut(u)$. Its image consists precisely of the outer automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of all boundary multitwist subgroups. Such an automorphism lifts if it preserves the associated profinite multicurve incidence. An inertia-preserving automorphism does preserve that incidence, by the commuting-twist characterization of simplices. These assertions hold for the continuous materialization and the strict pro-object alike.

statement: The decorated two-level boundary tower has automorphism group $\GT$. Let $\mathcal T^{\partial}_{4,5}$ consist of $\widehat T_4,\widehat T_5$, all five forgetting functors, clutching inclusions with their $\widehat T_3,\widehat T_4$ factors, and coherent relabelling pseudo-actions. Its automorphisms are continuous equivalences fixing labelled stratum types, preserving oriented boundary inertia with one exponent $\lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times$, and commuting with these operations through natural isomorphisms satisfying their coherence equations. Modulo coherent natural isomorphism, \[ \pi_0\Aut(\mathcal T^{\partial}_{4,5})\simeq\GT. \tag{F.11} \] The same holds for the strict pro-objects. The coordinate identification uses the usual marking by oriented loops $x,y$ around $0,1$ and a compatible tangential base point. Changing the marking conjugates this description; the outer tower and arithmetic action are independent of these choices.
notes: Common cyclotomic exponent and coherent symmetric-group action are explicit. Galois surjectivity onto this group remains E.8.

statement: The full genus-zero boundary tower and its arithmetic subgroup. Let $\mathcal T^{\partial}_0$ contain all $n\geq3$ with the same decorations and all forgetting and clutching functors. Restriction is an isomorphism \[ \pi_0\Aut(\mathcal T^{\partial}_0) \xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_0\Aut(\mathcal T^{\partial}_{4,5}) \simeq\GT. \tag{F.12} \] F.10 gives the usual faithful arithmetic inclusion $G_{\Q}\hookrightarrow\GT$. Equating its image with all automorphisms is the open equality E.8. The categorical group thus identifies the early normalizer-type group E.7; the revised arithmetic-image group is the subgroup E.2.

statement: Completion for the elliptic types retains stack isotropy. For $(g,n)=(1,1),(1,2)$ take Jansen's labelled stable-curve category in exit variance, with a finite skeleton indexed by stable labelled dual graphs. Its strict completion F.2 is a category in profinite sets, faithful on discrete Hom-sets, and equivalent to the profinite-multicurve transporter category for $\widehat P_{g,n}$. At $\sigma$, \[ 1\longrightarrow\prod_v\widehat P_{g_v,n_v} \longrightarrow\Aut_{\widehat C_{g,n}}(\sigma) \longrightarrow A_\sigma\longrightarrow1, \tag{F.13} \] where $A_\sigma$ is the finite image of the discrete stabilizer on the dual graph and half-edges, fixing the original marked legs. No splitting is chosen. These categories carry F.9--F.10's finite constructible-sheaf comparison and outer Galois action, now for moduli \emph{stacks}.

statement: The precise remaining positive-genus automorphism comparison. We have not established that the automorphism group of the two elliptic boundary categories, forgetting, and all boundary clutchings is $\GT$. The precise comparison asks whether restriction from the decorated procongruence outer tower E.13 to this diagram is an isomorphism, with identical oriented inertia and relabelling data. Injectivity requires detection at these levels; surjectivity requires extension of every such pair to the full decorated tower. We do not claim that existence of $\GT$ actions in positive genus remains open: E.12--E.13 give current results and their exact morphism collections.

statement: The rational operadic analogue and its exact limitation. Over a characteristic-zero field $k$, define the rational analogue to be the parenthesized braid groupoids completed relative to their finite permutation quotients, with pure braid groups replaced by their Malcev prounipotent completions. Retain operadic composition, strand deletion and doubling, the braid symmetry, and the distinguished oriented inertia. Their structure-preserving automorphism group is $\mathrm{GT}(k)$. In the parenthesized chord-diagram realization it is $\mathrm{GRT}(k)$; an associator compares the realizations. The four- and five-point constraints are the symmetry equations and pentagon, and the identity-multiplier Lie algebra is the weight completion of $W=\mathfrak{grt}_1$. The exact sources are \citet[\S\S5--6, Propositions 5.1 and 5.5]{Drinfeld1990} and \citet[Proposition 3.4, Theorems 1--3, Corollary 4.1]{BarNatan1998}.

statement: A stronger higher-completion comparison is not assumed. One can also ask whether the nerve of the strict finite-category pro-object F.7, as a pro-object of stratified spaces, equals the full profinite stratified $\infty$-category $\operatorname{Gal}(X_{n,\C}/P_n)$. This requires comparison for all finite homotopy types and their constructible gluing, beyond finite sets. We do not establish it here. The first nontrivial test is $n=4$, whose boundary gluing retains a two-dimensional unstratified homotopy class even though its stratum groups are free.
